contains: Long Term Idle (LTI) of Train A

researcher_notes: PRIMARY source found on third pass: Badak LNG's own official corporate milestone page ('Tonggak Sejarah', portal.badaklng.co.id, Wayback snapshot 2018-06-15) records the dated event '2013 January 14 -- Long Term Idle (LTI) of Train A'. This is the ONLY per-train shutdown milestone the company ever published, and Train A never returned to service; IGU 2019 ('two presumed decommissioned in the early 2010s') and IGU 2020 ('trains A and B in decommissioning status') corroborate the era but not the year. Wikipedia's 'since 2011' narrative cites this same Badak page, which does NOT actually say 2011 -- the prior passes' dead end is resolved: the real company-logged year is 2013. Caveat for the data team: the dated 2013 event is the START of permanent Long Term Idle (the shutdown); formal decommissioning followed later without any announced date, so 2013 is staged as the best-supported retirement year. Tier medium: single strong primary (company's own history page); no second independent publisher states the year (Wikipedia is a derivative of the same page).

No dated public event exists for Train B's shutdown -- third pass exhausted the primary channel. Badak LNG's own official milestone page (Wayback, archived 2018-06-15 and 2019-01-21, covering through end-2017) records 'Long Term Idle (LTI) of Train A -- January 14, 2013' as the ONLY train-shutdown milestone in the company's history; there is NO corresponding entry for Train B, i.e. the operator itself never logged a dated B shutdown through end-2017 (page went 404 by Feb 2019). Indonesian government (DJKN, Jul 2021), ESDM/Pertamina releases, Badak Sustainability Report 2019 (full 16MB Wayback capture, text-searched), Bloomberg Technoz/CNBC/detik/Sindonews reactivation coverage 2023-2025, and Energy Intelligence (Mar 2016) all describe B only as 'nonaktif/decommissioned' with no year. Best bound: B stopped after A's Jan-2013 LTI and before the C/D wave IGU dates to end-2018; IGU 2019 lumps A+B as 'presumed decommissioned in the early 2010s'. Conclusion for data-team discussion: B's shutdown was apparently absorbed into progressive feed-gas-driven idling without a formal per-train announcement -- suggest either mirroring A's evidence qualitatively (early 2010s, no year) or recording a 2013-2018 range.

No train-specific dated idle event exists for Train E -- and the third pass shows why: E is Badak's designated ready-reserve ('siaga'/standby) train, cycling between occasional operation and standby as feed gas allows, so different publications simultaneously class it as operating, active, or standby. GIIGNL 2021 lists 4 trains (E-H); S&P Global (Jan 2021, Wayback) says only TWO trains actually operated through all of calendar 2020 with 'a third on standby' (unnamed); Indonesian Ministry of Finance DJKN (Jul 2021) confirms 2 of 8 trains functioning; Bloomberg Technoz (Oct 2023) has 'train E yang siaga untuk beroperasi'; Pranala (Aug 2024) calls E one of three ACTIVE trains while CNBC Indonesia (Aug 2024) quotes 'dua (train) jalan, satu standby (yaitu train) E'; LNG Prime (May 2026) again counts three of eight operational. Unlike Train F (which Badak's president director explicitly dated: last operated 2020), no company, government, or press statement ever assigns a year to E's idling. Conclusion: capacity was reduced by rotating E in/out of service without a formal idle declaration -- a defensible single idle-year does not exist; recommend the data team treat E's idling as undated (circa 2020-2021 crunch, intermittently active since).

contains: F yang memang kita desain untuk dihidupkan kembali

researcher_notes: Train F idled in 2020 -- resolved on third pass via Indonesian-language press. Bloomberg Technoz (Aug 13, 2024) quotes Badak LNG's president director on Train F: 'train itu terakhir beroperasi pada 2020' (that train last operated in 2020) and 'Kita lakukan preservasi sejak 2020' (we have preserved it since 2020). Independently, Sindonews (Oct 16, 2025) reports the Train F reactivation as 'reaktivasi fasilitas yang telah tak dioperasikan sejak 2020' (facility not operated since 2020). Both URLs verifier-PASSED with the year and train-specific tokens. Consistent context: Badak's Sustainability Report 2019 (Wayback full capture) still records a Train F startup during 2019, and S&P Global (Jan 2021) reports only two trains operating by then. F has been in 'extended short-term idle status (ESTI)' under preservation since 2020, and is the train Eni's North Hub FID (Mar 2026) will reactivate (target ~2028).
